Presenting LD 31 "An Act Regarding School Enrollment for Military-connected Students"

Joint Standing Committee on Education and Cultural Affairs

Wednesday, February 5, 2025

Senator Rafferty, Representative Noonan Murphy, and members of the Education and Cultural
Affairs Committee. My name is Senator Brad Farrin I am here today to present LD 31, An Act
Regarding School Enrollment for Military-connected Students and ask for your support.
As you are aware, military families face unique challenges that often require frequent relocations. This bill provides much-needed flexibility to ensure that military-connected students can continue their education at the school of their choice, which is crucial for their emotional,
mental, and academic well-being.
Military families have to make significant sacrifices to find housing, secure jobs, and navigate the various stresses that come with constant moves. One of the most difficult challenges is
ensuring that children receive a consistent, high-quality education despite these relocations. For
many military families, the added burden of changing schools can be overwhelming, especially when it comes to issues like childcare and medical or special needs services for their children.
This bill allows school superintendents to approve the transfer of a military-connected student
from one school administrative unit to another, giving families more flexibility in managing the
education of their children. It allows military-connected students who are in kindergarten
through grade 8 to continue in their current school for the remainder of the school year if their residence changes, and high school students in grades 9 to 12 to continue in their current school through graduation if their residence changes. This flexibility can be crucial for maintaining a sense of stability for students.
If we can help alleviate some of the stress that military families experience through this bill, then we should do so. If a student's best option is to stay in a school in Kennebec County instead of transferring to a school in York County, we should support that choice, provided the family can make it work.
I had the opportunity to meet with Melissa Willette, the New England Regional Liaison for the
Department of Defense, and Laura Cyr from the Department of Education to discuss this bill and collaboratively work on the amendment before you today. This amendment ensures that all parties are in agreement. I urge you to support this legislation, which will provide militaryconnected students with the option for stability and continuity in their education, allowing them to remain in the school of their choice.
Thank you for your time and consideration.

TESTIMONY IN SUPPORT OF
L.D. 31
AN ACT REGARDING SCHOOL ENROLLMENT FOR MILITARY-CONNECTED STUDENTS
February 5, 2025
Senator Rafferty, Representative Noonan Murphy and members of the Education and Cultural Affairs Committee. I am Eileen King, deputy executive director for Maine School Management Association, testifying on behalf of the legislative committees of the Maine School Boards Association and Maine School Superintendents Association in support of L.D. 31.
Our associations believe this bill is an important step to ensure that children of our military members receive the educational stability and continuity they deserve.
According to the Department of Defense, the child of an active military member may be required to move six to nine times from kindergarten through 12th grade. And each of those moves can mean uprooting a child from their home and support system, adding substantial stressors to their relationships, social lives and potentially impeding their academic progress.
Our schools work as hard as possible to support military-connected students: acting quickly to enroll students, assessing prior coursework, and providing them with the necessary academic and extracurricular supports to ensure they succeed in their new schools.
We believe this bill would offer more educational stability to the more than 1,200 military-connected students in our state, providing them with the consistency and support they need to reach their academic goals. We urge you to vote "ought to pass" on L.D. 31. Thank you.

The MPA Legislative Committee is neither for nor against LD 31. As
school administrators we want to make sure that any transfer is in
the student's best interest. This bill will allow for the continuation of a student's placement in a particular school even if the student's
family member is in the military and a move is necessary.
Upon reading the bill, there were many questions that arose that is causing us to not be in full support of the bill. Question such as: how
does this differ from a regular superintendent's agreement that could be available for any student; is there a travel time or distance
limit; and who is responsible for transportation? We would also
encourage the language of "shall" to "may" on Section 2. D. Without
answers to these questions, we cannot be in full support.
For these reasons, the MPA is Neither For Nor Against LD 31.

LD 31 -- An Act Regarding School Enrollment for Military-Connected Students

Chairman Rafferty, Vice Chair Murphy and honorable members of the committee; the Department of
Defense is grateful for the opportunity to support the policies reflected in LD 31, which aims to
increase access to flexible enrollment options for military families with school-age children.

My name is Melissa Willette, and I am the New England Region Liaison at the United States
Department of Defense-State Liaison Office, operating under the direction of Under Secretary of
Defense for Personnel and Readiness. We represent the Department and establish relationships with
state leaders across the country who are concerned for troops and their families' welfare by
harmonizing state and federal law on policy problems of national significance. These are identified by the Office of the Secretary of Defense, the Military Departments, and the National Guard Bureau as
areas where states can play a crucial role.

Military families are at a disadvantage when it comes to enrollment options available to their children, due to the timing of military directed moves. Military families move frequently and change school systems upwards of ten times prior to graduation. In addition to planned Permanent Changes of Station (PCS) moves across state lines, military families often experience additional subsequent relocations from temporary to permanent housing due to limited availability of military or community housing at
the time of their arrival.

LD 31 expands on previous efforts Maine has made to support military families by enhancing
flexibility and improved access to existing state and district open enrollment policies. With approximately 1700 active-duty service members, and 1300 active-duty children attending school in Maine, this committee has an opportunity to have a highly impactful and positive effect on the educational experiences of military children and families.

We thank the committee for considering this important legislation and are especially grateful for the
tremendous effort Maine has historically made in supporting our service members and their

families. We thank the Chair for taking up this legislation, the bill sponsor, Senator F arrin, for his

past and current advocacy on behalf of military families, and the co-sponsors, Senators Daughtry,

Haggan and Stewart for their support.
